publications.explanation:
For this 2023 paper, the recorded official-key answer is A, National Statistical Office (NSO). The relevant distinction among the options is the statistical organisation within MoSPI: the 2019 restructuring brought CSO and NSSO together under NSO. [MoSPI's restructuring clarification](https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1572847&lang=2&reg=48).

Be precise about the wording “compile Poverty Estimates”: collecting household-consumption data and estimating poverty are different tasks. A [24 July 2023 parliamentary reply](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/260/AU471.pdf?source=pqars) attributes the 2011–12 poverty-line and poverty-ratio estimates to the Planning Commission, using NSSO survey data. Do not learn from this question that MoSPI alone determines every poverty measure.

Update — checked 14 November 2026: MoSPI's [order effective 14 October 2024](https://mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/iss-circular/Restructuring%20Order%2014-10-2024.pdf) directs its divisions to use National Statistics Office (NSO) in communications, replacing NSSO/CSO terms. Separately, [HCES 2023–24 results released on 30 January 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2097601&lang=2&reg=48) provide consumption data used in poverty analysis; survey results are not themselves a single poverty-line estimate. These later developments supplement the historical answer.
